components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Discover how Earth recycles its water through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.title: Evaporation
components.body: The sun heats up water in rivers, lakes, and oceans, causing it to turn into water vapor and rise into the air.

components.title: Condensation
components.body: As water vapor rises higher, the cool air causes it to cool down and turn back into tiny liquid water droplets, forming clouds.

components.title: Precipitation
components.body: When too much water has condensed, the water droplets in the clouds become too heavy to stay in the air. They fall back down to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

components.title: Worked Example: A Puddle on a Sunny Day
components.body: Consider a puddle on the sidewalk after a rainstorm. Over the course of a few hours of sunshine, you notice the puddle shrinking and eventually disappearing.
components.takeaway: Evaporation in Action: Heat energy from the sun transferred to the water molecules, giving them enough energy to break free into the atmosphere as vapor.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor using heat from the sun?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process where liquid water absorbs heat and transforms into gas/vapor.

questions.question: Which phase of the water cycle directly forms clouds?
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapor condenses into tiny droplets that gather to form clouds.

questions.question: When water droplets in clouds become too heavy, what happens?
options: They turn into solid ice caps
questions.explanation: Gravity causes the heavy droplets to fall back to Earth as rain, snow, or other forms of precipitation.
